subject: DPA amendment: model-improvement exclusion, subprocessors, and cross-border evidence
messages:
From: Sarah Evans <sarah.evans@clearwellhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Todd <michael.todd@clearwellhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA amendment: model training & export controls

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal at Clearwell has reviewed the standard DPA and a few items jumped out where we need stronger guarantees before we can sign the pilot SOW. Primary asks are: a firm "no-training" commitment for tenant data (model improvement exclusion), a clear list of subprocessors and any planned transfers outside the US, and a short operational proof pack (SOC2 snapshot + proof that prompt/response content is not retained for training).

I attached our redlines (Clearwell_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf). Can Redwood provide: 1) proposed DPA language for no-training; 2) the current subprocessor registry and planned additions; 3) an ops evidence mini-pack and an estimate of how long it would take to produce the packets?

We also need to know how prompt/response ownership is treated — Clearwell wants confirmation that outputs and prompts are considered customer content and not used for model improvement.

Appreciate a quick turnaround; the pilot kick-off is scheduled for 06/10.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Legal Operations
Clearwell Health

Attachment: Clearwell_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Evans <sarah.evans@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA amendment: model training & export controls

Hi Sarah — thank you for the redlines and the clear asks. We can do a firm no-training commitment for tenant data used in the pilot and provide a subprocessor registry and the ops materials you requested.

Quick notes:
- We will propose an explicit clause that restricts any model improvement/training on customer-provided prompts/responses for the duration of the pilot (and include operational controls).
- Subprocessor list: I'll attach a current registry and note planned on-ramps.
- Ops evidence: we can produce a minimal evidence pack (SOC 2 snapshot, retention policy excerpt, and a short runbook showing data flow and KV/ephemeral caching behavior). Expect a 5–7 business day turnaround for the formal packet and legal language.

Next steps I'd suggest:
1) I will share Redwood's proposed DPA language for the no-train clause by end of day Thurs.
2) David (privacy) and Kimberly (legal) will review and confirm ops/evidence scope.
3) Marissa (AE) will coordinate DocuSign/HubSpot routing once redlines are agreed.

If Clearwell needs an interim operational assurance (e.g., onshore routing or KMS residency) we'll flag what we can commit to for the pilot.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_list_202805.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA amendment: model training & export controls

Folks — looping Priyom for ops evidence and runbook pieces. Action items:
- Priyom: please pull the lightweight ops evidence mini-pack (SOC2 snapshot, retention policy excerpt, ephemeral KV caching diagram, and a short note on how we disable model updates on the tenant path). Convert to a single PDF (ops_evidence_mini-pack.pdf). Target: 5 business days.
- Kimberly: I'll draft the proposed DPA language for the explicit no-training clause (will include scope, duration, and audit rights).
- Marissa: prepare the HubSpot/DocuSign route once we have agreed text. Also confirm what concessions (if any) we can include re: onshore routing/KMS.

Sarah's ask on prompt/response ownership: recommend we propose that outputs and prompts remain customer's content, and we add an explicit operational statement that customer content will not be used to update model weights or the training corpus. Kimberly, can you add an enforceable verification step (e.g., annual attestation or a right to request the evidence pack within X days)?

Thanks,
David
Director, Privacy Engineering
